# v0.6.0

The review API is now a four-rung ladder (`fetch_page`, `iter_pages`,
`iter_reviews`, `fetch`), with a real async twin for every entry point.

This is a large break: 37 API changes. It also fixes several bugs that produced
wrong data silently, five ways a credential or a reviewer's details could leak,
and two ways a hostile endpoint could exhaust the process.

## Breaking

| # | Change | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `httpx>=0.28,<0.29` is a runtime dependency | Add it if you pin strictly |
| 2 | `Review.country` and `Review.title` are `str \| None` | Add a `None` check; they were `""` |
| 3 | `FetchError.kind` is required; `country` widens to `str \| None` | Pass `kind=` if you construct one |
| 4 | `ReviewProvider` needs `afetch_page` and `source` | Add both to custom providers |
| 5 | `sort=OLDEST`/`RATING` with `limit` return the correct N | Results change; requests increase |
| 6 | `app_reviews.utils.*` removed | Use the store's own search client |
| 7 | `ReviewConfig`/`ExportConfig`/`ProxyConfig`/`load_config` removed | Pass `auth=`, `proxy=`, `retry=` directly |
| 8 | All four provider classes renamed | `RSSProvider` -> `AppStoreScraperProvider`, etc. |
| 9 | Normalisation and detection helpers removed | - |
| 10 | Serialised output uses `null`, not `""` | Handle `null` downstream |
| 11 | Play scraper: an empty envelope is a parse error | Was an empty page |
| 12 | Search clients raise `HttpError` on transport failure | Catch it |
| 13 | A malformed body yields a classified error, not a crash | - |
| 14 | `fetch`/`iter_pages` surface errors they used to swallow | Check `result.errors` |
| 15 | Play scraper is global, not per-country | `countries=` is ignored (and warns) |
| 16 | `ReviewProvider.countries()` gone | The client decides; see the source table |
| 17 | Clients take `http=`, not `timeout`/`proxy`/`retry` on providers | - |
| 18 | `BaseSearch` is now the `SearchClient` protocol | Drop the inheritance |
| 19 | Exceptions carry `status`; the class *is* the kind | `except RateLimitError`, not `err.kind` |
| 20 | `to_dicts()` is JSON-safe; `raw` opt-in | Pass `include_raw=True` if you need it |
| 21 | Every internal module moved | Import from `app_reviews` |
| 22 | `lookup_metadata()`/`alookup_metadata()` removed | `AppStoreSearch().lookup(...)` |
| 23 | The exporters removed | `to_dicts()` + your own writer |
| 24 | `FetchResult.errors`/`retryable` are derived properties | Read-only now |
| 25 | Exceptions have no `kind` attribute | Branch on the type |
| 26 | `CountryOutcome.elapsed` is required | - |
| 27 | Tokens refresh instead of freezing per client | - |
| 28 | `Review.country` uses one alphabet | Connect's `"USA"` becomes `"us"` |
| 29 | `http=` with `proxy=`/`retry=` raises | Configure the `HttpClient` you pass |
| 30 | Play scraper no longer fabricates `updated_at` | Dates were 1970-2001; refetch |
| 31 | `created_at`/`updated_at` both nullable; `is_edited` gone | Read `review.dated_at` |
| 32 | `raw` is unwrapped, and may be a `list` | `review.raw["entry"]` becomes `review.raw` |
| 33 | Google key failures raise `AuthError`; `token_uri` is checked | Catch `AuthError` |
| 34 | `capabilities()` and `SourceCapabilities` removed | See [how the sources differ](../../docs/reference/capabilities.md) |
| 35 | `StopReason` gains `"stalled"` and `"max_pages"` | Widen any exhaustive match on it |
| 36 | `countries=` is normalised and deduplicated | `["US", "us", "USA"]` now walks one storefront, not three |
| 37 | `GooglePlaySearch.lookup()` returns a real `version` when Play publishes one | Was always `"Varies with device"` |

On 34: `capabilities()` was added and removed inside this release. Of its seven
fields the library read two, one had the same value for every source, and one
described a reply API this package never calls. "How do these sources differ" is
a question you have while writing code, so it is answered in the docs instead.
`client.source` and `client.resolve_countries([...])` cover what remained.

## Fixed

Bugs that returned wrong data without saying so:

- **A featured Google Play search result was discarded on every query**: its id
  slot is empty, so searching for an app did not return that app. It now carries
  a real `rating_count` too.
- **`googleplay_scraper` dated every review to 1970-2001**, reading a protobuf
  nanos field as epoch seconds.
- **The Developer API dated an undated review to the epoch** instead of skipping
  it. `updated_at` is the only date this source reports, so `sort` and `since`
  read it.
- **`iter_reviews(since=...)` yielded the boundary page's older reviews**, up to
  200 of them. `fetch` filtered them; the stream had nothing to.
- **`iter_reviews(limit=N)` under-returned** on a source without a newest-first
  guarantee, counting reviews fetched rather than yielded.
- **`GooglePlaySearch.lookup()` invented an app** (`name="Unknown"`,
  `rating=0.0`) for a page it could not read.
- **A page of unusable RSS entries ended the walk** as `"exhausted"`.
- **One country raising discarded every country that had already walked.**
- **A repeated cursor walked forever.** A source handing back a page token it had
  already given out now ends the walk with the new `StopReason` `"cycle"`.
- **A source that never stopped issuing cursors walked forever, and `limit` could
  not stop it.** `limit` and `since` are both driven by reviews actually seen, so
  an endpoint returning empty pages with fresh page tokens escaped both: a caller
  who passed `limit=5` still walked without end. Three consecutive review-less
  pages now end the walk as `"stalled"`, and a `10,000`-page ceiling reports
  `"max_pages"`. The ceiling also bounds the cursor set the walk retains to detect
  cycles, which grew without limit alongside it.
- **`Retry-After: nan` retried with no backoff at all.** It parses as a float and
  every comparison against NaN is False, so the clamp returned `0.0` and a
  throttled client fired its whole retry budget back to back. An unusable value
  now falls through to the exponential schedule. A negative delay and a past date
  still mean "now", as documented.
- **`GooglePlaySearch` reported no version for any app.** Play does publish one for
  some apps, on the detail page. Verified against the live `us` storefront:
  Firefox publishes `153.0.1`, Spotify and Duolingo publish nothing.
- **`fetch(sort="newest", limit=N)` raised `AttributeError`.** `Sort` is a
  `StrEnum`; the equivalent string now works everywhere.
- `limit=0` yielded one review, and a negative limit sliced from the wrong end.
- An out-of-range timestamp raised `OverflowError` out of `fetch_page`, which
  `iter_pages` documents it does not do.
- `close()` released only one of the two connection pools.
- A malformed URL burned the whole retry budget before reporting.
- Five async examples in the docs were `SyntaxError` and could not be run as
  printed. Every Python block in the docs is now parsed by the test suite.

## Security

- **`app_id` was interpolated unescaped into three URL paths**, two of them on
  requests carrying a bearer token, so `..` segments retargeted them.
- **The Google token exchange followed redirects.** A 307 re-sends the POST body
  (the signed assertion) to the next host. httpx strips `Authorization`
  headers on an origin change; it cannot strip a body.
- **`repr()` of either credentials model emitted the full private key**, so it
  reached tracebacks and any error reporter that captures locals.
- **Key material stayed readable in traceback frame locals** even once `repr` was
  fixed. A reporter reads the *locals* of every frame and follows `__cause__`, and
  the loaders bound the raw `.p8`, and the entire service-account document, in the
  frame that raised. No failure path leaves either reachable from the error now.
- **A response body was read into memory with no size limit**, so an endpoint
  answering with an endless stream grew the process until it died. Bodies are
  streamed against a `32 MiB` cap. `timeout` is per socket operation and cannot
  bound an exchange, so an attempt also gets a `120s` wall-clock ceiling: a server
  answering each read just inside the read timeout used to hold a worker open
  indefinitely.
- **`token_uri` accepted any `*.googleapis.com` host**, a shared multi-tenant
  namespace. Now an exact allowlist.
- **All four providers logged whole review entries** on a parse failure,
  including reviewer names and review text. They log the review id.
- The Connect cursor is checked for scheme, host, port, path and control
  characters; `idna` is upgraded past CVE-2026-45409.

## Added

- **`Retry-After` is honoured**, and outranks the exponential schedule. New
  `RetryConfig.max_backoff` (default 60s) caps both it and the backoff, which
  previously grew without bound.
- **`iter_reviews()`** streams across countries holding one page at a time.
- **Async twins** for every entry point, on real `httpx.AsyncClient` I/O.
- **Connection pooling**: a ten-page walk costs one TLS handshake, not ten.
- **`CountryOutcome`** per country: pages, reviews fetched, elapsed, and
  `stopped_because`.
- **`concurrency=`** bounds the cross-country fan-out.
- **`since`** reduces the number of requests, not just what you see.
- **`AppMetadata.current_version_release_date` and `first_release_date`**, on both
  stores. iTunes already sent both in the response this package parses, so they
  cost no extra request. Both are `datetime | None`: a date has no honest
  placeholder, and a sentinel would sort and filter as though it were real.
  Precision differs, so compare across stores with that in mind. The App Store
  sends a real timestamp; Play publishes only the day it renders, so a Play date is
  midnight UTC on that day. A Play *search* hit carries neither; use `lookup()`.
- **`countries=` accepts any collection of `Country` or `str`**, so the region
  groups (`Country.ALL`, `Country.EUROPE`, and the rest) can be passed directly.
  They are `frozenset`s and did not type-check against the old `list[str]`.
  Entries are normalised and deduplicated, so alpha-3 and mixed case collapse.
- **`country=` on both search clients accepts a plain string.** `Country` is
  Apple's 155 storefronts, and Play serves markets it omits (Serbia, Bosnia,
  Morocco) which were previously unreachable under a type checker.
- **`max_bytes` and `max_duration` on `HttpClient`**, and `MAX_PAGES` on the review
  clients, for callers who need different ceilings than the defaults.

## Upgrading

Most callers only touch three things: catch `AuthError` around client
construction, read `review.dated_at` instead of `review.created_at`, and drop
`countries=` on anything but the public App Store RSS feed.

If you store fetched data, note items 30 and 32: Google Play dates before this
release are wrong and worth refetching, and `raw` changed shape for that source.

Two walks that used to run without end now stop and say so, as `"stalled"` or
`"max_pages"` (item 35). If you branch on `stopped_because`, treat both as "more
data may exist" alongside `"limit"` and `"cycle"`, and resume from the last
cursor. Anything that read `"exhausted"` as "we have everything" was already
wrong for `"limit"`, `"since"` and `"cycle"`, and is now wrong for two more.

Field-by-field reference: [docs/reference/models.md](../../docs/reference/models.md).
Per-source behaviour: [docs/reference/capabilities.md](../../docs/reference/capabilities.md).
